entities.summary:
Louis-Marie-Florent de Lomont d'Haraucourt, marquis later duc du Châtelet, was a French aristocratic general and diplomat.

Born in Semur-en-Auxois, Burgundy, France on November 20, 1727, he would go on to serve as a key figure in the French military during the Seven Years' War.

As a skilled military strategist, du Châtelet played a crucial role in the French victory at the Battle of Fontenoy in 1745, securing a significant French victory against the British and their allies.

However, du Châtelet's significance extends beyond his military prowess, as he also served as a diplomat and played a key role in the French Revolution.

Du Châtelet's legacy continues to be felt today, with his contributions to the development of modern diplomacy and military strategy remaining relevant in the modern era.

As he once said, 'The only way to achieve greatness is to set objectives that are beyond your reach.'

Du Châtelet's remarkable life and achievements serve as a testament to the power of determination and vision.
